introduction: To protect computers and sensitive data from hackers, malware, and network threats, specific 'Security Measures' are deployed. In Tier-1 competitive exams, direct questions are framed around the basic definitions and primary functions of these defensive tools.

core_concepts.title: Antivirus
core_concepts.description: A type of 'Utility Software' designed specifically to search for, detect, and remove software viruses and other malicious software (malware) that have already entered the computer system. (Examples: Norton, McAfee, Windows Defender, Quick Heal).

core_concepts.title: Firewall
core_concepts.description: The 'Security Guard' or 'Gatekeeper' of a computer network. It monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules. Its absolute primary function is to establish a barrier that prevents 'Unauthorized Access' to a private network.

core_concepts.title: Encryption
core_concepts.description: The process of converting normal, readable data (like a password or a message) into an unreadable, scrambled 'Secret Code' so that even if a hacker steals the data, they cannot understand it.

core_concepts.title: Decryption
core_concepts.description: The exact reverse process of encryption. It is the conversion of encrypted data (the secret code) back into its original, readable format using a specific 'Key'.

important_entities.name: Unauthorized Access
important_entities.significance: This is the most critical keyword for Firewalls. If an exam question asks what prevents 'Unauthorized Access' from the internet, the answer is always Firewall.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants frequently confuse the two. Remember the distinction: A **Firewall** stands at the door and blocks bad traffic from entering the network. An **Antivirus** scans the inside of the house (the computer files) to catch and kill malware that somehow managed to get in. A firewall does NOT scan files for viruses.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: A Wall of Fire between you and the Internet
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Visualize a literal wall made of fire that separates your safe local network from the dangerous, unpredictable public internet.

exam_strategy_tips: In SSC CGL Tier-1, you will inevitably see the question: 'Which of the following is used to protect a network from unauthorized access?' Without hesitation, select 'Firewall'.
